subject: Post-call recap — multi-pool strategy, isolation needs & SLA exceptions
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Tang <aisha.t@novagen.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — multi-pool strategy, isolation needs & SLA exceptions

Hi Aisha — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed path forward. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency variability on long-tail requests (inference P95 spikes to ~3s under current infra).
- Regulatory requirement: PHI-containing inference must never leave the customer VPC; audit logs retained 7 years.
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume batch reranking workloads (peak token throughput expected in Q1).

Goals we aligned on:
- Dedicated, isolated pools for PHI workloads with VPC peering and KMS control.
- Predictable 99th percentile latency at <= 250ms for short-form generation (seq len ~512).
- A pilot (2 weeks) to validate performance, then month-to-month committed pool with ability to scale on forecasted spikes.

Proposed technical scope (initial):
- 2 dedicated GPU islands (1x canary pool with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, 1x production pool initially 12x GPUs).
- Tenant isolation via single-tenant pools + private control plane (Redwood Private).
- Autoscale policy: baseline 30% capacity reserved, burst up to 2x for 20% of daily traffic; graceful fallback to smaller model variants for non-PHI requests.
- SLOs: 99% requests < 250ms; 99.9% < 500ms for production pool; 99.99% availability SLA for reserved capacity (enterprise tier).

Risk notes / open technical questions:
- Quantized model parity: Novagen needs acceptance criteria for 8-bit/4-bit quantized model output quality. We should run a small eval suite during pilot.
- Cold-start behavior for large KV caches — we recommend warmup traffic plan during pilot window.
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide current artifacts but any gap for on-prem controls will require a short compliance checklist.

Commercial / timeline asks:
- Ballpark committed monthly spend for the proposed production pool (12 GPUs): we'll provide a preliminary quote once procurement requirements are clear.
- Pilot: we can spin up the canary pool within 48–72 hours after contractual LOI. Two-week validation window.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Novagen to confirm acceptable pilot dates and any procurement constraints (PO vs. contract).
2) Redwood to send a one-page pilot MOP + draft mutual action plan (attached), and a rough cost estimate for the 12x production pool.
3) Schedule a short ops runbook call with Marcus (cc'd) and your infra lead to align on VPC peering and KMS.

Attachments: novagen-dedicated-scope-20261108.pdf (scope summary), mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (editable MAP).

Thanks — I'll follow up with a crisp MAP and quote.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0196
From: Aisha Tang <aisha.t@novagen.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novagen Procurement <procure@novagen.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — multi-pool strategy, isolation needs & SLA exceptions

Thanks for the recap, Sergio — this is helpful and captures the main points. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot timing: week of Nov 22nd would work for infra availability (we need the canary pool up by EOD Nov 23).
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence is required, but because PHI will be processed we need an addendum describing retention, KMS key ownership, and audit log export cadence. Can you confirm Redwood’s retention window options (we may request 7 years as noted)?
- Cost: procurement asked for a ballpark monthly figure to include in our internal budget packet. A per-GPU-month estimate (plus network egress assumptions) will be enough for now.

Two small asks to include in the MAP:
1) A short acceptance test for quantized model output (we'll provide a 250-example prompt set).
2) A rollback/fallback clause describing what happens if the pilot fails to meet the 99% < 250ms target (what remediation or credits apply).

If Redwood can send the MOP + cost figures by EOD Friday (Nov 12), we'll aim to get procurement sign-off and return a stainable LOI/Purchase Order quickly.

Cheers,
Aisha
Head of ML Ops
Novagen Labs
aisha.t@novagen.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — multi-pool strategy, isolation needs & SLA exceptions

Looping in ops notes for the MAP and pilot plan. Key confirmations from infra/ops: 
- Canary pool (4x A100-eq) can be provisioned in 48 hours; we will tag instances for warmup and pre-load KV cache using a small synthetic load.
- We can document KMS flow to support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) and export audit logs to the Novagen logging endpoint every 24 hours. Retention options: 90 days (default), 1 year, 7 years (legal addendum required).
- SLO enforcement: we'll instrument a test harness for the 250-example prompt set Aisha will provide; acceptance will be measured against median and 99th latency and output similarity thresholds (we should define exact PSD/ROUGE thresholds with product).

Open items for commercial/legal:
- Rollback credits: recommend 10% credit of monthly committed spend for pilot failure to meet the 99% latency target (placeholder for negotiation).
- Network egress: we need to call out egress assumptions in the quote (typical enterprise practice).

I'll draft the ops section of the MAP and share an internal checklist. Sergio — let me know if you want me to include a short playbook for warmup traffic and cache priming.

-Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — multi-pool strategy, isolation needs & SLA exceptions

Appreciate the quick reply, Aisha. We'll do the following and aim to get the MAP + ballpark quote to you by EOD Friday (Nov 12):

Our deliverables this week:
- Draft MAP with pilot timeline, acceptance criteria (quantization eval plan), rollback/credit language, and commercial assumptions (Marcus to add ops runbook).
- Preliminary cost estimate: per-GPU-month for the 12x production pool + canary pricing and egress assumptions.
- DocuSign-ready two-week pilot agreement (link below) — sign to start provisioning.

Proposed immediate actions for Novagen:
1) Confirm pilot window week-of-Nov-22 and provide the infra lead contact for the runbook call.
2) Share the 250-example prompt set and any model output quality constraints you want used in the quantization acceptance tests.
3) Let procurement know we will include a 10% pilot-failure credit placeholder; final number negotiable.

DocuSign (pilot LOI): https://www.docusign.com/novagen/provisioning-agreement
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NOVA-2026-0911

I'll follow up with the MAP attached and a short cost note by Friday. Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Sergio

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (will follow with Marcus' ops addendum)
